detail.longDescription: I am deploying Apache Superset 6.1.0 and checking its cache configuration. My live runtime is configured like this: CACHE_CONFIG = NullCache DATA_CACHE_CONFIG = NullCache FILTER_STATE_CACHE_CONFIG = SupersetMetastoreCache EXPLORE_FORM_DATA_CACHE_CONFIG = SupersetMetastoreCache RESULTS_BACKEND = None So the app is not using Redis or Memcached. But Superset 6.1 still includes flask-caching in its dependency set, and I am trying to understand whether this package is still required even when the runtime uses: NullCache SupersetMetastoreCache My questions are: Is flask-caching still required by Superset 6.1 even if Redis/Memcached are not configured? Is SupersetMetastoreCache still implemented through Flask-Caching? Can flask-caching be removed safely from the runtime requirements if only NullCache and SupersetMetastoreCache are used? If not, what part of Superset 6.1 depends on it? We observed Flask-Caching versions blocked in our mirror with 403, across the 2.x line, including 2.5.1 down through 2.0.2 and this prevents image build. Can the community please confirm - Whether this dependency is still expected in 6.1, Whether there is a supported way to avoid it, and What the recommended Redis/Memcached setup is if we need those backends? What I already checked I verified the live runtime config inside the container. I confirmed there is no Redis backend configured. I confirmed there is no Memcached backend configured. I confirmed flask-caching is still pinned in the Superset requirements template.
